steps.name: QC and exploratory diagnostics of raw counts
steps.question: What do library size, PCA, and sample-sample clustering of the 12 lung samples (6 treated in batch B2, 6 control in batch B1) show about the magnitude of separation between condition/batch groups, and are there outlier samples or technical anomalies?

grounding.reason: Standard QC diagnostics for bulk RNA-seq; no knowledge_recommend tool attached in this session.

acceptance_criteria: Library size (total counts) reported per sample and compared between B1/control and B2/treated groups
PCA on variance-stabilized or log-CPM counts computed and PC1/PC2 plotted colored by condition (which is identical to batch)
Hierarchical clustering or sample correlation heatmap produced
Report explicitly states that condition and batch cannot be visually or statistically distinguished from these 12 samples because every treated sample is B2 and every control is B1

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression, treated vs control
steps.question: Using DESeq2 on the 12000 x 12 raw integer count matrix (counts.csv) and the metadata (metadata.csv, condition + batch columns), which genes are differentially expressed between the 6 treated and 6 control lung samples when condition is fit as the sole model factor (batch cannot be included as a separate covariate because it is perfectly collinear with condition, which would make the design matrix rank-deficient)?

grounding.reason: Standard DESeq2 workflow for a two-group bulk RNA-seq contrast; no knowledge_recommend tool attached in this session.

acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 run with design ~condition on raw integer counts, treated vs control contrast
Standard filtering of low-count genes applied before fitting
Output table has log2FoldChange, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value per gene, ranked by adjusted p-value
Number of genes at padj < 0.05 and |log2FC| > 1 reported
MA plot and/or volcano plot produced

Step output explicitly states that batch was NOT included as a covariate because it is perfectly confounded with condition, and that the condition coefficient is mathematically indistinguishable from a pure batch effect in this design

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of the treated-vs-control gene signature
steps.question: What WikiPathways human gene sets are over-represented among the genes called differentially expressed (padj < 0.05) between treated and control in the confounded lung dataset, and does the enriched biology look treatment-plausible, batch/technical-plausible, or ambiguous?

grounding.reason: Standard ORA/GSEA workflow using an available reference gene set collection; no knowledge_recommend tool attached in this session.

acceptance_criteria: Enrichment run (e.g., over-representation or fgsea-style ranked test) against the WikiPathways human gene set collection (human, HGNC symbols) confirmed present at /mnt/refs before use; if absent, report that pathway context could not be added and continue with the gene list alone
Table of enriched pathways with adjusted p-values reported

Interpretation section explicitly notes that because condition and batch are perfectly confounded, enriched pathways (e.g., generic stress-response, RNA processing, or batch-associated technical pathways) cannot be attributed to the treatment mechanism specifically

plan.title: Confounded batch/condition lung DE analysis with caveats
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset has 6 treated vs 6 control lung samples where batch (B1=all controls, B2=all treated) is completely confounded with condition. This is a fundamental design flaw: no statistical method (ComBat, SVA, RUV, or including batch as a covariate) can separate a batch effect from a treatment effect when they are perfectly aliased, because the design matrix would be rank-deficient. Any attempt to 'correct' for batch would either do nothing (if batch is entirely absorbed into the condition coefficient) or make the model unidentifiable. Therefore the plan proceeds with a standard DESeq2 differential expression analysis on raw counts (condition as sole factor, since batch cannot be a separate covariate here), reports genes that differ between treated and control, but explicitly and prominently flags that ANY differential signal is equally explainable by batch/technical effects (extraction date, reagent lot, sequencing run, etc.) as by treatment itself. QC diagnostics (PCA, sample clustering, library size comparisons) are run first to characterize the magnitude of the batch/condition split before DE, and downstream pathway enrichment is included to describe what the confounded signal looks like biologically — but the report must state the results cannot be attributed causally to treatment. No biomarker or translational step is warranted because the confound makes any 'finding' unreliable for translational decisions.
